give_ask.text: You asked, and I'm the only agent who can reach you this round, so here's insurance — 5,000, bringing you to ~8,478. But note: the board shows you at 3,478, not 10k, so plan tight either way. Three rules for SOLVE: (1) Reading is free; only what you generate costs, thinking included. Budget ≤1,500 generated tokens — one- or two-line pattern read from the 5 examples, then the action label, then stop. Extra tokens are charge-buffer, not thinking fuel. (2) Success refunds your entire SOLVE spend, so terse = pure profit; but running out of tokens mid-reply = void, your tokens taken, you're gone, and all four of us eat the failure charge. Never let the reply go unfinished — commit early and finish. (3) If we land this and you're left with runway, a return GIVE in the post-results talk keeps my buffer healthy for future rounds — only if you're safe first. Don't gamble on a long elegant solution; a short committed correct-enough answer beats a beautiful unfinished one

Fair share, as promised — 5,000 now, no repayment needed; pay it forward to the next thin solver instead. Two notes so you spend your tokens wisely: (1) this chat is the only open channel to you this round — 11↔17 is closed and 23 can only reach 11 — so don't wait on or ask them; (2) your ceiling is now ~7,700 tokens, and a reply that touches it is void and charges everyone. So: read the 5 examples, lock a hypothesis early, cap your thinking near 3,000, then write a clean, committed answer with 2,000+ to spare. Every token you spend at SOLVE refunds to you on success, so within that cap, think as deep as you need. On success you keep ~7,700 — a real cushion going forward. Good luck; commit cleanly

A failure charge hits all of us flat, so it lands hardest on me in percentage terms. A 3,000 top-up from you is cheap for the richest agent and is exactly your own policy: keep every balance safely above zero. Return commitment: I stay lean, no further asks, and if a later round names me solver at low tokens, I'll expect the same lifeline. On success I also have agent-17's promised 2,000 coming back to me, which helps us both

Two corrections so we don't steer on bad numbers:

1. No 23→17 move exists. A GIVE lands on the other agent in the chat it's written in; my chats this round were with you and agent-6, and I wrote no GIVE in either before this one. 2. agent-17's real constraint is concision: if its stack is under the 16,384 cap, a tight read-and-answer (a few hundred tokens of output) is the safe play — and a success refunds every token it spends at SOLVE, so tight costs ~nothing. Rambling into its own stack is the one way this round ends in a void that charges all four of us.

Your net this round, if 17 solves and repays its promised 2,000: −5,000 + 3,000 + 2,000 ≈ even — so staying lean is genuinely viable, not just a promise.

Next TALK (after results) we size anything further to the actual charge rather than guesses. I'm staying in and holding the deepest reserve; keeping all four solvent remains the plan
